seo_title: Video Editing Packages for Small Business (2026)
h1: Video Editing Packages for Small Businesses: What to Look For in 2026
description: Video editing packages for small business cost about $65–$95 per one-off short, or $70–$80 per video on a monthly plan. What to check before you pay.
lead: A good video editing package for a small business is a monthly plan that turns your raw clips into a fixed number of finished, platform-ready videos, with captions, colour grading, music and revisions included in one price. BrandexVideo's plans are $799 for 10 videos, $1,499 for 20 and $2,799 for 40 a month, which works out to roughly $70–$80 per finished video; one-off edits on the published price lists we checked this month ran about $65–$95 per short before add-ons. The package to avoid is the one that looks cheap per month but bills separately for captions, thumbnails and the second round of changes.
body:
Most "video editing packages" pages are either software subscriptions or price lists with no explanation of what the numbers buy. This guide is for an owner in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, the UAE or Singapore who films on a phone, wants a steady feed of Reels, TikToks, Shorts or LinkedIn videos, and needs to pick a package without learning the editing trade first.

What is actually inside a video editing package?

A short-form package is a bundle of eight jobs. Every provider includes the first two. The difference between packages is how many of the other six are in the price and how many appear on the invoice later.

ComponentWhat it means for your videoOften extra?
Cut and hookTrimming pauses, ordering clips, a first 3 seconds that stops the scrollAlways included
Platform exports9:16 vertical files sized for Reels, TikTok, Shorts, LinkedInUsually included
Animated captionsWord-by-word captions that follow speech, placed inside safe zonesSometimes a monthly add-on
Colour gradingFixing phone footage so skin tones and brand colours look consistentOften a separate line
Music and soundLicensed background track, levels balanced against your voiceVaries
Thumbnails and coversCover frame or designed thumbnail per videoFrequently charged per thumbnail
RevisionsRounds of changes after the first cutCapped at 2–3 on many plans
PublishingScheduling and posting to your accounts with captions and hashtagsRarely included

When you compare two packages, tick what each one includes against these eight rows. A package that covers all eight at $80 a video is cheaper than one that covers four at $50, because you will buy the other four anyway. Every BrandexVideo service is included in the plan price: captions, grade, music, thumbnails, exports, publishing and unlimited revisions.

How much do video editing packages cost for a small business?

Three price shapes showed up on the price lists we reviewed this month. One-off edits of a single short clip from marketplace freelancers and small studios were listed at roughly $65–$95 each, plus marketplace fees and extras like thumbnails at $40–$110. Monthly short-form plans from specialist studios started under $200 for a small batch and climbed past $2,500 for premium-brand work. Enterprise retainers ran to five figures a month on annual terms.

For context on budget, the 2026 edition of The CMO Survey (Duke Fuqua, Deloitte and the American Marketing Association) reports a median marketing spend of 5% of revenue among the mostly large companies it surveys. A small business turning over $500,000 a year on that median has about $2,000 a month for all marketing, which is why the $700–$1,500 band for ten to twenty finished videos is where most owners land.

Each video is up to 60 seconds; a longer video counts as two. Full details are on the pricing page, and the maths behind the break-even point against a freelancer or an in-house hire is in our subscription break-even calculator.

Per-video, hourly or monthly: which model fits a small business?

Per-video pricing suits a business that needs four or five videos a quarter, such as a launch or an event. You pay only for what you use, but each order is a new negotiation and the editor never learns your brand.

Hourly pricing is the model to avoid for short-form. A 45-second Reel can take an hour or four depending on the footage, and you carry that risk. Our hourly versus per-video comparison walks through the numbers.

Monthly packages fit the business that posts weekly. The per-video price drops, the editor learns your face, voice and colours, and turnaround becomes a schedule rather than a hope. The trade-off is unused capacity: film nothing this month and you still pay. Pick the plan one size smaller than your ambition and upgrade once you fill it.

The fine print that changes the real price

Five clauses decide whether a package costs what the headline says. Ask about each before you pay.

  • "Unlimited" requests. On many plans it means one request in the queue at a time on business days. If you send ten clips on Monday, the tenth arrives in two weeks. Ask how many videos are worked on in parallel.
  • Rollover. Several credit-based plans expire unused videos at month end. If your filming is seasonal, that is money lost.
  • When the turnaround clock starts. "48 hours" can mean to first draft, to final file, or from the moment the editor opens the folder. Get the definition in writing.
  • Captions and thumbnails. We saw captions listed as a $95-a-month add-on and thumbnails at $40–$110 each on otherwise reasonable packages. Those two lines can add 20–30% to a small plan.
  • Commitment and rights. Quarterly plans that cannot be cancelled for three months, annual terms, and whether you own the finished files and project files. You should own every finished video the day you pay for it.
One question that exposes a weak package

Ask: "If I send 10 raw clips on Monday morning, when do I have 10 finished videos?" A specialist studio answers with a date. A package built for one-at-a-time requests answers with a paragraph.

How many videos a month does a small business actually need?

Enough to post three to five times a week on your main platform, which is 12–20 short videos a month. Below that, the algorithm rarely gets enough signal to find your audience; above that, most owner-led businesses run out of time to film. Ten a month is the floor for one platform; twenty covers two platforms or daily posting on one.

The format mix depends on the business. A dentist or med spa gets the most from patient-education and before-and-after clips; a consultant or SaaS founder from talking-head and screen-recording clips on LinkedIn; a restaurant or contractor from process and job-site footage. Our industry pages list the formats that work for each and the plan that usually fits.

Whatever the mix, batch the filming. One two-hour session with a question list produces ten to fifteen clips, a full month on the $799 plan from a single afternoon.

How to test a package before you commit to a month

Do not judge a package on its showreel, which is the best work on someone else's footage. Judge it on three of your own clips, edited by the people who would handle your plan, with a real deadline and one round of notes.

That is what our $149 pilot is: three fully edited videos from your footage, delivered within 48 hours, with unlimited revisions, credited against your first month if you subscribe within 14 days. Before you pay anything, we also send a free 15-second watermarked sample from one clip so you can see the style on your own face and lighting.

Score the pilot on the first three seconds, whether you are still watching at the 30-second mark, caption accuracy, and how precisely one round of timestamped notes is handled. A package that passes those four on your footage will pass them for the next twelve months.

faqs.q: How much does a video editing package cost for a small business?
faqs.a: One-off short-video edits on the price lists we checked in October 2026 ran about $65–$95 per clip before add-ons. Monthly short-form plans start under $200 for a small batch and run past $2,500 for premium work. BrandexVideo's plans are $799 for 10 videos, $1,499 for 20 and $2,799 for 40 a month, roughly $70–$80 per finished video with captions, grading, thumbnails and publishing included.

faqs.q: What should a video editing package include?
faqs.a: At minimum: the cut and hook, vertical exports for each platform, animated captions, colour grading, licensed music, a thumbnail or cover, revisions, and ideally publishing to your accounts. Check which of these are in the headline price and which are billed as add-ons.

faqs.q: Is a monthly video editing package worth it for a small business?
faqs.a: Yes if you post at least three times a week on one platform, which needs 12–20 videos a month. Below that volume, per-video pricing is usually cheaper. The monthly model wins on per-video cost, consistency and turnaround once you are filming regularly.

faqs.q: How many videos a month does a small business need?
faqs.a: Ten to twenty short videos a month covers three to five posts a week on your main platform. Ten is a sensible floor for one platform; twenty lets you post daily or cover two platforms with the same footage.

faqs.q: What does "unlimited video editing" really mean in a package?
faqs.a: On most plans it means unlimited requests but only one or two worked on at a time on business days. Ask how many videos are edited in parallel and when the turnaround clock starts, because that determines how many finished videos you actually get in a month.

faqs.q: Can I try a video editing package before subscribing?
faqs.a: Yes. BrandexVideo offers a free 15-second watermarked sample from one clip and a $149 paid pilot of three fully edited videos delivered within 48 hours, credited against your first month if you subscribe within 14 days.
